thread:
maria: Quick thought: we need a small, consistent Auth adapter interface for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
ajay: +1 but don't force a single token format. adapter should translate into a canonical claim envelope.
kevin: Keep adapter surface tiny: Verify(token) -> bool, Extract(token) -> canonical-claims, Introspect(optional) -> meta.
sam: Dedicated customers want project-bound API keys that carry routing hints. adapter must preserve passthrough fields like `binding` or `aud`.
emily: Also: legacy 1.x keys. We need ordered fallback: legacy -> jwt -> mTLS. adapters should chain, not replace.
ajay: Implementation idea: define a proto and offer both a library shim and a sidecar gRPC service. proto sketch:
```proto
service AuthAdapter {
  rpc Verify(VerifyRequest) returns (VerifyResponse);
  rpc Extract(ExtractRequest) returns (ExtractResponse);
}
```
kevin: Important: ban policy logic in adapters. RBAC mapping must be a separate service that consumes canonical claims.
maria: Example canonical envelope (normalized):
```
sub: "svc-12345"
iss: "redwood-inference"
tenant: "org:acme"
actor_type: "service"
roles: ["model:invoke","billing:view"]
exp: 1700000000
binding: "project:prod-1"
```
ajay: Adapters must forward provenance headers: x-request-id, x-auth-path, x-auth-adapter so audits keep origin.
emily: Rollout plan: library shim for Hosted/Dedicated first, then sidecar for Private/VPC. easier to migrate clients.
sam: Ops: audit events must record adapter type and any fallback used. do not lose provenance.
auth-bot: NOTE: created ticket INF-9999 to prototype adapter proto + shim (assigned: eng-platform).
kevin: Decision proposal: standardize on adapter proto + minimal JSON envelope; adapters do translation only; RBAC mapping is separate. Rollout: lib shim -> test Hosted -> sidecar for Private.
maria: +1. ajay will own proto + lib; emily + sam for fallback and telemetry test matrix.
emily: I'll open a draft PR with proto + shim tomorrow.
sam: I'll draft test cases for legacy keys, jwt, and mTLS.
kevin: :thumbsup:
maria: thanks, let's keep the adapter surface minimal and the RBAC surface expressive.
